## What's happening

- **Instagram Releases Updated 2026 Guide to Creating Reels**: Instagram has published an updated guide for 2026 covering everything from recording and editing your first reel to using Remix, Collab, and syncing transitions to trending sounds. ([updated 2026 guide to creating reels](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
- **TikTok Adds AI Creator Search to TikTok One**: TikTok is integrating AI Creator Search into TikTok One to help brands filter creators based on audience, niche, and past performance. The platform also reported that creator content achieves 52% higher click-through rates than non-creator content. ([AI Creator Search](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
- **YouTube to Introduce Gemini Chat Editing for Shorts in 2027**: YouTube plans to allow creators to edit Shorts by simply chatting with Gemini starting in 2027. ([Gemini in 2027.](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
- **LinkedIn Research Shows B2B Buyers Research Months Before Speaking to Sales**: New data shared via LinkedIn highlights that B2B buyers start exploring solutions 124 days before speaking to a seller, with buying decisions driven primarily by groups. ([B2B buyers](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
- **Meta Unveils 'Jolly' Totem for Muse Voice and Avatar Stack**: Meta has packaged its real-time voice and avatar stack into a pocket-sized totem called Jolly, allowing users to interact with the Muse agent via a fingerprint sensor without opening an app. ([Labubu-ification of Meta’s Muse](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
- **LinkedIn Tests Advanced Creator Discovery Filters**: LinkedIn is testing advanced creator discovery within Creator Marketplace, introducing search filters for content type, industry, audience demographics, and Top Voices ahead of an early 2027 rollout. ([advanced creator discovery](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
- **YouTube Testing Shorts Series Feature**: YouTube is testing a new Shorts Series feature designed to help users organize their short-form videos into episodic and serialized content. ([Shorts Series](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
- **Instagram Rolls Out 'Kits' in Instagram Edits**: Instagram Edits is rolling out 'Kits' which allows users to save custom colors, text styles, caption styles, and audio. ([Instagram Edits](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
- **YouTube Adds GIF Commenting for TV Viewers**: YouTube is upgrading its comment section for users watching on TV by introducing the ability to comment using GIFs. ([comment section](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
- **Delta Air Lines to Launch an Advertising Business**: Delta Air Lines is planning to launch an internal media network and has hired Keri Paison to lead it, following a trend of non-retail brands building out retail media networks. ## Content ideas for social media

1. **Why B2B Buying Decisions Take Months Longer Than You Think** (Thread) - Essential context on B2B sales cycles based on newly released LinkedIn platform research.
   - New insights show that B2B buyers start exploring solutions a full 124 days before ever speaking to a seller.
   - Purchasing choices are rarely made by individuals; they are driven entirely by groups.
   - Reaching six or more contacts before a deal appears in your CRM increases win rates by 17 percentage points.
   - Engaging three or more contacts during the active cycle adds another 16 points to your win rate.
   - Despite this, 76% of LinkedIn ad spend targets director-level roles, completely missing the wider buying group.
2. **Gen Z Demands Authenticity: The Power of Brand Bloopers** (Carousel) - Why highly polished brand videos are losing steam and unpolished content is winning.
   - AI can create almost anything at the click of a button, making polished content feel boring and generic.
   - Audiences are actively craving real moments, behind-the-scenes setups, and genuine human error.
   - 19% of consumers overall want to see more behind-the-scenes content from brands.
   - That desire climbs even higher to 26% among Gen Z audiences.
   - Sharing missed lines, laughter, and bloopers reminds people that your brand is run by real humans, not robots.
3. **Holiday Ecommerce to Smash Records at $275B** (Infographic) - Urgent macroeconomic outlook for holiday marketers based on Adobe Analytics data.
   - Adobe Analytics predicts U.S. online retail sales will hit a record $275.1 billion this holiday season.
   - This projection marks a solid 6.7% year-over-year increase.
   - The impressive growth is expected to happen despite consumer sentiment tumbling and ongoing consumer strain.
   - There are only 13 Mondays left until Christmas, meaning brands need to lock in their holiday strategies now.
4. **Is Your Brand Utilizing TikTok's AI Creator Search?** (Short video) - A quick tactical breakdown of TikTok's newest creator tool and what its performance stats mean for ad budgets.
   - Hook: Wondering how top brands are finding high-performing creators on TikTok instantly?
   - TikTok is introducing AI Creator Search directly inside TikTok One to filter creators by audience, niche, and past performance.
   - Along with AI search, TikTok One Pay is launching to handle invoicing and pay creators within 30 days while keeping 100% of earnings.
   - Data shows creator content on TikTok secures a 52% higher click-through rate than non-creator content.
   - Closing CTA: Are you shifting your ad budget toward creator-led content yet? Let us know in the comments.
5. **The VMAs Hit an 11-Year High Viewership** (Poll) - Capitalizing on the massive spike in award show viewership driven by pop culture giants.
   - Poll Question: Which major factor drove you to tune into the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards?
   - Option 1: Taylor Swift's massive cultural pull
   - Option 2: Madonna's landmark performances and wins
   - Option 3: Snoop Dogg hosting the night
   - Context: The 2026 VMAs drew an impressive 8.4 million viewers on CBS, marking a 51% increase and an 11-year high.
6. **What's New in Social: Meta's Jolly Totem & YouTube's Gemini Shorts** (Newsletter) - A fast-paced platform update roundup covering Meta's hardware push and YouTube's upcoming AI tools.
   - Meta has taken its Muse voice and avatar stack into a pocket-sized totem called Jolly, operable via a fingerprint sensor without opening an app.
   - YouTube announced plans to let creators edit Shorts by simply chatting with Gemini starting in 2027.
   - YouTube is also testing a new Shorts Series feature to help users organize episodic and serialized content.
   - Instagram Edits is rolling out 'Kits' allowing users to save custom colors, text styles, caption styles, and audio.
   - LinkedIn is testing advanced creator discovery search filters for content type, industry, audience demographics, and Top Voices.
